{{Short description|Elliptic analog of hypergeometric series}}
In mathematics, an '''elliptic hypergeometric series''' is a series <math>{\textstyle \sum c_n}</math> such that the ratio <math>{\textstyle \frac{c_n}{c_{n - 1}}}</math> is an [[elliptic function]] of <math>n</math>, analogous to [[generalized hypergeometric series]] where the ratio is a [[rational function]] of <math>n</math>, and [[basic hypergeometric series]] where the ratio is a periodic function of the [[complex number]] <math>n</math>.  They were introduced by Date-Jimbo-Kuniba-Miwa-Okado (1987) and {{harvtxt|Frenkel|Turaev|1997}} in their study of elliptic [[6-j symbol]]s.

For surveys of elliptic hypergeometric series see {{harvtxt|Gasper|Rahman|2004}},  {{harvtxt|Spiridonov|2008}} or {{harvtxt|Rosengren|2016}}.

==Definitions==
The [[q-Pochhammer symbol]] is defined by 
:<math>\displaystyle(a;q)_n = \prod_{k=0}^{n-1} (1-aq^k)=(1-a)(1-aq)(1-aq^2)\cdots(1-aq^{n-1}).</math>
:<math>\displaystyle(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_m;q)_n = (a_1;q)_n (a_2;q)_n \ldots (a_m;q)_n.</math>
The modified Jacobi theta function with argument <math>x</math> and [[nome (mathematics)|nome]] <math>p</math> is defined by
:<math>\displaystyle \theta(x;p)=(x,p/x;p)_\infty</math>
:<math>\displaystyle \theta(x_1,...,x_m;p)=\theta(x_1;p)...\theta(x_m;p)</math>
The elliptic shifted factorial is defined by
:<math>\displaystyle(a;q,p)_n = \theta(a;p)\theta(aq;p)...\theta(aq^{n-1};p)</math>
:<math>\displaystyle(a_1,...,a_m;q,p)_n=(a_1;q,p)_n\cdots(a_m;q,p)_n</math>
The theta hypergeometric series <math>{\textstyle _{r + 1}E_r }</math> is defined by
:<math>\displaystyle{}_{r+1}E_r(a_1,...a_{r+1};b_1,...,b_r;q,p;z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{(a_1,...,a_{r+1};q,p)_n}{(q,b_1,...,b_r;q,p)_n}z^n</math>
The very well poised theta hypergeometric series <math>{\textstyle _{r + 1}V_r }</math> is defined by
:<math>\displaystyle{}_{r+1}V_r(a_1;a_6,a_7,...a_{r+1};q,p;z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{\theta(a_1q^{2n};p)}{\theta(a_1;p)}\frac{(a_1,a_6,a_7,...,a_{r+1};q,p)_n}{(q,a_1q/a_6,a_1q/a_7,...,a_1q/a_{r+1};q,p)_n}(qz)^n</math>
The bilateral theta hypergeometric series <math>{\textstyle _r G_r }</math> is defined by
:<math>\displaystyle{}_{r}G_r(a_1,...a_{r};b_1,...,b_r;q,p;z) = \sum_{n=-\infty}^\infty\frac{(a_1,...,a_{r};q,p)_n}{(b_1,...,b_r;q,p)_n}z^n</math>

==Definitions of additive elliptic hypergeometric series==

The elliptic numbers are defined by 
:<math>[a;\sigma,\tau]=\frac{\theta_1(\pi\sigma a,e^{\pi i \tau})}{\theta_1(\pi\sigma ,e^{\pi i \tau})}</math>
where the [[Jacobi theta function]] is defined by
:<math>\theta_1(x,q) = \sum_{n=-\infty}^\infty (-1)^nq^{(n+1/2)^2}e^{(2n+1)ix}</math>
The additive elliptic shifted factorials are defined by
*<math> [a;\sigma,\tau]_n=[a;\sigma,\tau][a+1;\sigma,\tau]...[a+n-1;\sigma,\tau]</math>
*<math>[a_1,...,a_m;\sigma,\tau] = [a_1;\sigma,\tau]...[a_m;\sigma,\tau]</math>
The additive theta hypergeometric series <sub>''r''+1</sub>''e''<sub>''r''</sub> is defined by
:<math>\displaystyle{}_{r+1}e_r(a_1,...a_{r+1};b_1,...,b_r;\sigma,\tau;z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{[a_1,...,a_{r+1};\sigma,\tau]_n}{[1,b_1,...,b_r;\sigma,\tau]_n}z^n</math>
The additive very well poised theta hypergeometric series <sub>''r''+1</sub>''v''<sub>''r''</sub> is defined by
:<math>\displaystyle{}_{r+1}v_r(a_1;a_6,...a_{r+1};\sigma,\tau;z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{[a_1+2n;\sigma,\tau]}{[a_1;\sigma,\tau]}\frac{[a_1,a_6,...,a_{r+1};\sigma,\tau]_n}{[1,1+a_1-a_6,...,1+a_1-a_{r+1};\sigma,\tau]_n}z^n</math>
